quiz.title: Module 3 — Tuesday — Storytelling Frameworks
quiz.description: Tuesday's quiz covers the CAT framework, how much context a short social story needs, what makes adversity land, what a takeaway should do, Freytag's Pyramid and its five stages, the purpose of the hook, and why the takeaway carries a story that converts.

questions.prompt: What does the CAT storytelling framework stand for?
questions.explanation: Context sets the scene, adversity supplies the difficulty, and the takeaway gives the reader something to carry away. Three parts, short enough for a caption.

questions.prompt: According to the video, how many sentences should you ideally use to set the context of a short social media story?
questions.explanation: Context has to be fast. A sentence or three is enough to orient the reader before the difficulty arrives, and anything longer loses them before the story starts.

questions.prompt: What is the most important element of the adversity stage in the CAT framework?
options: Giving a long explanation of the character's background
Focusing on one specific challenge or difficult moment
Ending the story with a question
questions.explanation: One concrete difficulty lands harder than a list of vague ones. Specificity is what makes the reader recognise their own situation.

questions.prompt: What should the takeaway stage of the CAT framework communicate?
options: A list of all the events that happened
The names of everyone involved in the story
A detailed description of the setting
One clear lesson or idea the audience can remember and apply
questions.explanation: The takeaway is the reason the story was worth reading. One clear lesson is memorable; several competing ones cancel each other out.

questions.prompt: Who invented Freytag's Pyramid, according to the video?
questions.explanation: Gustav Freytag, a nineteenth-century German playwright and novelist, set out the five-part dramatic structure that still carries his name.

questions.prompt: Which of the following correctly identifies the five stages of Freytag's Pyramid as explained in the video?
options: Introduction, rising action, climax, falling action, takeaway
questions.explanation: Introduction, rising action, climax, falling action and the closing beat. The shape rises to a turning point and then resolves.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the hook in Freytag's Pyramid?
options: To explain every detail of the story
To make the audience stop scrolling and become interested in the story
questions.explanation: The hook buys the reader's attention for the rest of the piece. It does not need to explain or resolve anything — it needs to make stopping worth it.

questions.prompt: Why is the takeaway considered one of the most important parts of a story that converts?
options: It makes the story longer and more detailed
It focuses only on the storyteller's achievements
It replaces the need for a strong hook
It gives the audience a lesson they can apply to their own lives
questions.explanation: A story converts when the reader sees something they can use. The takeaway is where the story stops being about the writer and becomes useful to the audience.
